title: Prepositions of time and place
subtitle: in, on and at for months, days, clock times, cities and exact spots

rows.example: I've left the tickets **in** the living room!
Sharon has been **in** the travel agent's for an hour!

blocks.intro: We also use **in** in these phrases:

blocks.text: With verbs of motion (come, go, move, run, walk, etc.), we usually use **to** instead of **in**, **on** or **at**.
blocks.note: Was it hot when you **went to** Japan?

rows.example: I got a new car **on** Saturday.
There are some useful Italian phrases **on** page 97.

rows.use: Place · on top of an object
rows.example: Did you put your car keys **on** the kitchen table?

blocks.intro: We also use **on** in these phrases:

blocks.text: We say **in** the morning/afternoon/evening, but **on** Monday morning / Wednesday evening, etc.

blocks.correct: We're flying to Washington **in the morning** / **on Tuesday morning**.
blocks.incorrect: We're flying to Washington **on the morning**.

blocks.text: We don't use a preposition with **tomorrow**, **yesterday**, **tomorrow morning**, **yesterday evening**, etc.

rows.example: There's a bus **at** ten past three.
What's it like **at** the North Pole?

rows.use: Place · buildings, when we are talking about the activities that happen there
rows.example: I think John is **at** the cinema, watching Titanic.
Rania isn't here. She's **at** a party.

blocks.intro: We also use **at** in these phrases:

blocks.text: Compare how we use **in** and **at** for places. We use **in** for larger areas that are all around us when we are there. We use **at** for smaller places and points on a journey.

blocks.correct: We're spending our next holiday **in** the countryside.

blocks.text: Let's meet **at** the train station. (a point we arrive at)

exercises.title: A · Correct the preposition
exercises.instruction: Write the correct preposition. If the preposition in brackets is already correct, write it again.

items.prompt: We first visited China ___ 2006. (on)
My birthday is ___ the second of July. (at)
Let's meet ___ five o'clock, shall we? (on)
School starts again ___ September. (in)
There's a party at Emily's ___ Saturday. (at)
What do you want to do ___ the morning? (on)
Let's go and see Grandma ___ Easter. (on)
Where do you usually go ___ Christmas Day? (in)
